recap.title: Seven projects. Four chapters of experience.
recap.description: Different products, a consistent approach: understand the problem, build with care and keep the evidence close.

items.question: What makes your work full-stack?
items.answer: My independent projects include frontend, server logic, data and deployment. XO Arena demonstrates an Express and Socket.IO backend; Emerald Case brings together data, authentication and checkout. My historic job titles remain frontend roles.

items.question: Which frontend systems do you work with?
items.answer: React, Next.js and TypeScript form the core. My work also includes rendering strategies, shared UI systems, real-time features, multilingual interfaces, PWA delivery and interactive Three.js experiences.

items.question: Which backend tools can you demonstrate?
items.answer: XO Arena uses Express, Socket.IO, Prisma and MySQL. Emerald Case uses Prisma and MongoDB alongside authentication, Stripe checkout and email. Each case study describes its own scope.

items.question: How do you use AI in engineering?
items.answer: I use AI as a supervised tool for implementation, exploration, code review and documentation. I remain responsible for architecture, security, checking the result and deciding what is ready to ship.

items.question: Can I explore this portfolio without 3D motion?
items.answer: Yes. Reading view presents the project and experience content without the immersive scene. Reduced-motion preferences and a non-WebGL path keep the essential links and information available.

items.question: What is your role at Hesabo?
items.answer: As a Senior Frontend Developer, I contribute to frontend architecture and delivery across Admin, Employer, Employee and Support surfaces, along with mentorship and PWA/Android work. This is collaborative product work, not sole ownership of the financial platform.

items.question: What does the 3D shop demonstrate?
items.answer: Sarochi is a spatial apparel-showroom concept with rack navigation, product galleries and a prepared photographic appearance preview. Purchasing continues at the official store. The preview is experimental; it does not establish exact fit or arbitrary photoreal human try-on.

items.question: Do you work from idea to deployment?
items.answer: Yes, within an agreed scope. My public projects demonstrate product implementation and deployment, while my employment experience adds collaborative architecture, review, release and mobile delivery.

items.question: How can we start a conversation?
items.answer: Share the product, the challenge and the outcome you need. Use the contact form or an existing direct channel, and we can discuss scope and the next useful step.

contact.title: Your next idea. Our first conversation.
contact.description: Tell me what you are building, where it gets difficult and what a good outcome looks like.
